Subject: Prostate Multiparametric MRI | Reporting Radiologist | 20 January 2025

Clinical Context: Assessment of rising prostate-specific antigen (11.4 ng/mL) alongside clinical suspicion for malignancy.

Findings: The gland occupies 54.66 mL of space. T2-weighted sequences highlight a discrete hypointense focus at the base-to-mid left peripheral zone, spanning roughly 18 × 14 × 12 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction with a corresponding low apparent diffusion coefficient. Dynamic contrast sequences capture early, focal enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is visible. Pelvic lymph nodes maintain normal size and structure.

Impression: PI-RADS 5 lesion located in the left peripheral zone (base/mid), approximately 18 mm in diameter. Prostate-specific antigen density calculates to 0.209 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability stands at 0.44734785.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Recent outpatient review addressed persistently high PSA values, climbing from 10.4 ng/mL last July to 11.4 ng/mL on the latest draw. The gentleman notes slight lower urinary tract symptoms yet explicitly rules out haematuria or skeletal pain. In light of the rising trend and his age, urology clinic assessment alongside multiparametric MRI scheduling was processed.
